functional.text: Starting from seed URLs, crawl the web: fetch HTML pages, store them, extract links and add new URLs to the frontier.
Avoid duplicate work: each URL is fetched once per cycle; pages whose content duplicates an earlier page are not stored or indexed twice.
Recrawl pages to keep them fresh, more often for pages that change often.
Expose stored pages to the indexing team for 6 months.

non_functional.text: Polite: at most 1 request/s per host and obey robots.txt (disallow rules, crawl-delay).
Throughput: 2B pages per month, scaling horizontally by adding fetchers.
Robust against crawler traps, slow servers and malformed HTML; no lost work when a machine dies.

assumptions.text: ~100 KB per HTML page; ~1/3 of fetched pages are copies or near-copies.

out_of_scope.text: Images/video, JavaScript rendering, building the search index itself.

api.notes: Internal control API; also used to force a recrawl.
Lets operators slow down or block a host after a complaint.

data.name: url_meta
data.fields: url_hash (PK), url, host, priority, last_fetched, next_fetch_at, content_hash, status, depth
data.why: Billions of rows, point lookups and updates by url_hash; drives recrawl (next_fetch_at).

data.name: frontier
data.fields: front queues by priority → back queues per host; heap of (host, ready_at)
data.why: Ordering and politeness live in the queue structure; persisted to disk with checkpoints.

data.name: pages
data.fields: blob key url_hash/fetch_time → compressed HTML + response headers, batched into large files
data.why: Write-once, read in bulk by indexing: ~1.2 PB raw for 6 months.

parts.title: URL frontier: politeness and priority
parts.problem: Decide which URL is fetched next so that important pages go first, no host sees more than 1 request/s (or its robots.txt crawl-delay), and thousands of fetchers still stay busy.

options.name: one global FIFO
options.cons: links cluster by site: hundreds of fetchers hit one host at once; no notion of importance

options.name: FIFO + each fetcher sleeps between requests
options.cons: doesn't stop two fetchers hitting the same host; idle fetchers

options.name: priority front queues → per-host back queues + ready-time heap
options.pros: importance decides what enters; one host is served by one fetcher at a time with an enforced delay
options.cons: more frontier machinery; must shard by host

parts.choice: priority front queues feeding per-host back queues, released by a politeness scheduler (heap of host → ready_at); robots.txt cached per host
parts.why: N1 is enforced by structure, not by fetcher discipline: a host is only handed out when its ready_at has passed. N2 comes from breadth: ~1,500 pages/s at ≤ 1/s per host means at least 1,500 hosts in flight, which per-host queues give naturally.

nodes.label: Politeness scheduler (per-host back queues, ready-time heap)

parts.title: Fetchers and DNS
parts.problem: Download ~770 pages/s (peak ~1,500) when each fetch takes ~1 s and some servers hang, without losing URLs when a fetcher dies.

options.name: thread per fetch, OS resolver
options.cons: ~1,500 threads per box, and the blocking system resolver becomes the bottleneck

options.name: async I/O fetchers + local caching DNS resolver
options.pros: thousands of fetches in flight per box; DNS answered from memory
options.cons: async code; must respect DNS TTLs

options.name: headless browser per page
options.cons: 10–100× the cost per page; out of scope (O1)

parts.choice: async HTTP fetchers that lease URLs from the frontier, with a caching DNS resolver per fetcher cluster and strict timeouts
parts.why: ≈ 1,500 concurrent fetches fit on a handful of async workers; DNS lookups (often 10–200 ms) are cached per host, and leases make a crashed fetcher's URLs reappear (N3).

parts.title: Dedup: seen URLs and duplicate content
parts.problem: Answer 'have we seen this URL?' for every extracted link out of 20B URLs, and 'is this page a copy?' for the 1/3 of pages that are copies or near-copies.

options.name: exact URL hash set in a database
options.cons: ~1 TB of keys and a DB lookup for every extracted link

options.name: Bloom filter over normalised URLs
options.pros: ~25 GB for 20B URLs at 1% false positives, in memory
options.cons: 1% of new URLs are wrongly skipped (acceptable)

options.name: content hash + SimHash fingerprints
options.cons: near-duplicate lookup needs bit-band indexing

parts.choice: URL normalisation + Bloom filter for seen URLs; exact content hash and SimHash fingerprints for duplicate content
parts.why: URL dedup stops refetching, which is most of the volume (each URL is linked many times). Content dedup keeps the 1/3 of copies out of storage and the index. A Bloom filter's false positive only skips a new URL, which is a cheap mistake.

parts.title: Parsing and content storage
parts.problem: Store ~1.2 PB of raw HTML for 6 months where indexing can reprocess it, and extract links without slowing the fetchers.

options.name: pages as rows in a database
options.cons: petabytes of blobs in a DB is expensive and slow

options.name: one object per page in blob storage
options.cons: billions of tiny objects: per-request cost and slow bulk reads

options.name: batch pages into large append-only files (WARC-style) in blob storage; parse from an event queue
options.pros: cheap, sequential bulk reads for indexing; parsing scales separately
options.cons: need an index (url_hash → file, offset)

parts.choice: fetchers append pages to large batched files in blob storage and publish a fetched-page event; parser workers consume it
parts.why: 1.2 PB written once and read in bulk is exactly what object storage is for, and batching avoids billions of small objects. A queue between fetch and parse lets each side scale and absorbs bursts.

parts.title: Recrawl scheduling and freshness
parts.problem: Spend a fixed fetch budget so news pages are refreshed hourly while static pages are visited rarely.

options.name: BFS order, fixed revisit interval
options.cons: wastes budget on static pages; news goes stale

options.name: importance × staleness priority with an adaptive interval per URL
options.pros: the budget follows value and change rate
options.cons: needs per-URL history and scores

options.name: sitemaps / change feeds only
options.cons: most sites don't publish them

parts.choice: importance × staleness priority with an adaptive revisit interval stored in url_meta; a recrawl scheduler re-enqueues due URLs
parts.why: Halve a URL's interval when its content hash changed and double it (up to a cap) when it didn't. Hourly news and monthly blogs then converge to their own rates without hand tuning.

deep_dives.title: Crawler traps

options.name: trust the link graph
options.cons: an infinite calendar or session-id URL space eats the whole budget of one host

options.name: limits: max depth, max URL length, page budget per host
options.cons: can cut off legitimately deep sites

options.name: detect repeating URL patterns / near-duplicate content per host
options.cons: heuristics need tuning

deep_dives.choice: hard limits (depth, URL length, pages per host per cycle) plus near-duplicate rate per host as a trap signal
deep_dives.why: N3: traps are unbounded URL spaces; a per-host budget caps the damage of any single one, and a host whose new pages are mostly SimHash-duplicates is demoted.

deep_dives.title: Fetcher crash mid-batch

options.name: delete URLs from the frontier when handed out
options.cons: a crash loses them for the whole cycle

options.name: lease with timeout, ack after the page is stored
options.cons: a page can be fetched twice after a crash (content dedup absorbs it)

deep_dives.choice: lease with timeout, ack after the page is stored
deep_dives.why: N3: losing work silently is worse than an occasional duplicate fetch, and P3 already drops duplicate content.

deep_dives.title: Finding near-duplicates fast

options.name: compare SimHash against every stored fingerprint
options.cons: billions of comparisons per page

options.name: split the 64-bit SimHash into bands and index each band
options.pros: only pages sharing a band are compared
options.cons: 4–8× the index size

deep_dives.choice: banded SimHash index: 4 bands of 16 bits, compare candidates by Hamming distance ≤ 3
deep_dives.why: Two pages within distance 3 must share at least one identical band, so the band lookup finds every candidate cheaply.

wrapup.bottlenecks: DNS resolution (local caching resolvers), the frontier (sharded by host hash so each host lives on one shard), the Bloom filter (partitioned by URL hash), and politeness itself: a few huge sites cap throughput, so breadth across hosts matters.
wrapup.failures: Fetcher crash: URLs are leased from the frontier and redelivered if not acked. Unhealthy host (5xx/timeouts): per-host exponential backoff. Traps: max depth, max URL length, page budget per host. Frontier shard loss: rebuilt from checkpoint + url_meta.
wrapup.monitoring: Pages/s fetched, error and timeout rate by host, frontier size and age, duplicate rate, robots.txt denials, DNS latency, bandwidth.
wrapup.scale: Add fetchers and frontier shards; place fetcher clusters in several regions close to the hosts they crawl (host-hash affinity).
wrapup.future: JavaScript rendering for dynamic sites, sitemaps and change feeds (push instead of poll), spam/link-farm detection.
